Aberration

ab-uh-RAY-shun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Aberration is something that departs from what is normal, usual, or expected, typically in an unwelcome way.

The star player's terrible performance was such an aberration that fans assumed he must have been injured.

Worked Example

Scientists initially dismissed the strange lab reading as a one-time aberration -- a glitch -- until it happened again the following week.

An aberration is a deviation from the norm, and it usually carries a sense that something has gone wrong or slipped from what's expected.

How Aberration Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

deviation

deviation: a departure from what is normal or expected

irregularity

irregularity: something that doesn't follow the normal pattern

Antonyms

norm

norm: the usual, expected standard

regularity

regularity: the quality of following a consistent, predictable pattern

How Strong Is It? — quirk → breakdown → aberration

quirk vs. aberration

quirk vs. aberration: A quirk is a small, harmless peculiarity in an otherwise normal pattern.

breakdown vs. aberration

breakdown vs. aberration: A breakdown is a complete failure or collapse of the normal pattern, even more extreme than an aberration.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — aberr-

root — aberr-: to wander away, stray (the same root as erratic, which you met earlier in this course) (Latin ab- 'away' + errare 'to wander')

suffix — -ation

suffix — -ation: the act, process, or result of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Aberration comes from Latin ab- ('away') + errare ('to wander') -- the same root behind erratic, which you already met earlier in this course. To aberrate, at root, is to 'wander away' from the expected path.

Use the root in a new word: erratic

Use the root in a new word: erratic: The storm made the ship's compass reading wildly erratic. (You met erratic earlier in this course, in the -ic morpheme unit.)

Root Check

Word Choice

Aberration nearly always carries a negative or at least unsettling undertone -- it flags something that has slipped from the normal pattern, closely related to the earlier word anomaly, but with a stronger hint that the deviation is unwelcome or troubling.
